questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply grammatical conventions to preserve clear relationships within sentences.
questions.prompt: Complete the sentence for formal written English: “Each of the exhibition stands ___ a separate number.”
questions.explanation: The head of the subject is the singular each. The plural noun stands is inside a prepositional phrase.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply grammatical conventions to preserve clear relationships within sentences.
questions.prompt: Choose the form that clearly puts the repair before the inspection: “By the time the inspector arrived, the caretaker ___ the lock.”
questions.explanation: The past perfect places the repair before another past event.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply grammatical conventions to preserve clear relationships within sentences.
questions.prompt: Which revision makes clear that Ada, rather than the bus, was crossing the road?
questions.answer: As Ada crossed the road, she saw the bus stop.
options: Crossing the road, the bus stopped where Ada could see it.
While crossing the road, the bus was seen by Ada.
As Ada crossed the road, she saw the bus stop.
The bus, crossing the road, stopped near Ada.
questions.explanation: The opening clause explicitly gives Ada as the person crossing.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply grammatical conventions to preserve clear relationships within sentences.
questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: “If the parcel had arrived yesterday, we ___ its contents before today’s meeting.”
questions.explanation: The condition describes an unreal past event, so its imagined past consequence uses would have plus the past participle.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply grammatical conventions to preserve clear relationships within sentences.
questions.prompt: What is the function of “until the rain eased” in “The team waited until the rain eased”?
questions.answer: It states the time up to which the team waited.
options: It states the time up to which the team waited.
It names the people who waited.
It gives the reason why the rain eased.
It identifies the place where the team waited.
questions.explanation: The clause sets the end point of the waiting period.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply grammatical conventions to preserve clear relationships within sentences.
questions.prompt: Which completion maintains parallel structure? “The workshop taught us to measure the timber, to mark the joint and ___.”
questions.explanation: The list uses parallel infinitives: to measure, to mark and to check.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply grammatical conventions to preserve clear relationships within sentences.
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a defining relative clause to identify the pupils who waited outside?
questions.answer: The pupils who had no identity cards waited outside.
options: The pupils, who had no identity cards, waited outside.
The pupils waited outside, and none of them had an identity card.
The pupils who had no identity cards waited outside.
All the pupils waited outside because some had no identity cards.
questions.explanation: The defining relative clause restricts the subject to the pupils without cards.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply grammatical conventions to preserve clear relationships within sentences.
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly reports a promise made on Monday about Tuesday: “I will return the drill tomorrow,” Musa said on Monday.
questions.answer: Musa said on Monday that he would return the drill the next day.
options: Musa said on Monday that I would return the drill the next day.
Musa said on Monday that he would return the drill the next day.
Musa said on Monday that he had returned the drill the day before.
Musa said on Monday that he returned the drill that morning.
questions.explanation: He refers to Musa. Would expresses the future from Monday’s viewpoint, and the next day means Tuesday.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use clues in surrounding text to select words or paraphrases that preserve meaning.
questions.prompt: “The office gave us a provisional date while it waited for the venue to confirm.” What does provisional mean here?
questions.explanation: The date is tentative until the venue confirms availability.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use clues in surrounding text to select words or paraphrases that preserve meaning.
questions.prompt: “Although the first response sounded promising, the organisers stopped short of making a commitment.” What did the organisers do?
questions.answer: They expressed interest without making a firm promise.
options: They expressed interest without making a firm promise.
They ended the event sooner than scheduled.
They promised to act but set no date.
They refused to discuss the proposal at all.
questions.explanation: Stopped short of signals that they did not take the final step of committing.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use clues in surrounding text to select words or paraphrases that preserve meaning.
questions.prompt: A note says, “The spare key is accessible only to staff on duty.” What does accessible mean here?
questions.explanation: The notice concerns who is allowed to obtain the key.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use clues in surrounding text to select words or paraphrases that preserve meaning.
questions.prompt: “The news was greeted with reserve: nobody objected, but nobody offered support.” What does reserve suggest?
options: A supply set aside for later
questions.explanation: The contrast between no objection and no support points to a restrained reaction.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use clues in surrounding text to select words or paraphrases that preserve meaning.
questions.prompt: Choose the most precise verb: “The auditor will ___ the claim by comparing the receipt with the bank record.”
questions.explanation: Comparing independent records is a way of checking whether a claim is accurate.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use clues in surrounding text to select words or paraphrases that preserve meaning.
questions.prompt: “The corridor was still after the bell, apart from the ticking of the clock.” Which word best replaces still?
questions.explanation: The exception identifies the only sound in an otherwise quiet corridor.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use clues in surrounding text to select words or paraphrases that preserve meaning.
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses waive correctly to mean voluntarily giving up a requirement?
questions.answer: The committee agreed to waive the entry fee for the visiting pupils.
options: The caretaker will waive to pupils from the gate.
The painter will waive the boards before applying paint.
The pupils agreed to waive the bus at the stop.
The committee agreed to waive the entry fee for the visiting pupils.
questions.explanation: Waive means to set aside a right, fee or requirement.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use clues in surrounding text to select words or paraphrases that preserve meaning.
questions.prompt: “The plan was ambitious, but the group scaled it back when two volunteers withdrew.” What happened to the plan?
options: It was put into action ahead of schedule.
Its cost was measured on a scale.
Its organisers made it more demanding.
questions.explanation: Scaled it back means reduced its size or scope in response to fewer volunteers.
